newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia 1996 RPI target in doubt after Oct rise.
newsitem.headline: Croatia 1996 RPI target in doubt after Oct rise.

text.p: Croatia's 1996 inflation target of up to three percent appeared in doubt after retail prices, propelled by goods and services, rose 0.6 percent in October but analysts said on Tuesday there was no reason to worry.
"Practically, whether inflation will be 3.0 or 3.5 percent matters very little," Zeljko Rohatinski of Zagreb's Economics Institute told Reuters.
"But there is nothing significant (in latest statistics) that could endanger a general trend," he added.
Zarko Miljenovic, chief economist at leading commercial bank Zagrebacka Banka, said he saw December-on-December rate at around 3.5 percent although the average inflation may be lower.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) in a study published this week also put this year's annual inflation at 3.5 percent.
But it forecast the 1997 rate higher, at 6.0 percent.

According to the figures released by the State Statistics Bureau, retail price inflation quickened to 2.9 percent in the first ten months this year with the year-on-year rise at 3.2 percent in October.
On a monthly level, goods prices were up 0.7 percent and services 0.4 percent.

But Rohatinski said this rise was marginal in view of the fact it was boosted by higher prices of agricultural produce, rather than industrial products and other items that form the index of officially monitored prices.
He also played down a 0.7 percent monthly increase in living costs. They were up 4.0 percent from October last year.
Producer prices were flat compared to September and rose only 0.6 percent from the same month last year. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
